source_text:
In sanctos Petrum et Paulum (homilia 13)
̔Ησυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγκώμιον εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους
ἀποστόλους Πέτρον καὶ Παῦλον.
1 Καλὸν μὲν τὸ ῥόδον, τῆς ἐαρινῆς ὥρας αὐτῷ προσφερούσης ὀσφραίνεσθαι,
ἀλλ' ἐὰν τῷ κρίνῳ συμπλακῇ εἰκότως εὐωδέστερον γίνεται· μύρον γὰρ μύρῳ
κιρνᾶται καὶ διπλῆ τῆς ἐντεῦθεν εὐω δίας ἀπόλαυσις γίνεται. Λαμπρὸς καθ' ἑαυτὸν ὁ
Πέτρος καὶ τῶν λαμπρῶν ὑπέρλαμπρος, ὡς ἀποστολικῆς ξυνωρίδος κορυ φεύς, ὡς
μαθητείας ὀφθαλμός, ὡς ὑπόμνημα ζήλου καὶ τῆς πίστεως πρόσωπον, ὡς σάλπιγξ
τοῦ μυστηρίου, ὡς γλῶσσα καὶ πολλὰς γλώσσας διδάξασα, ὡς ποιμὴν ἀνέγκλητος,
ὡς κυβερνή της ἄϋπνος, ὡς ἀπλανὴς ἡνίοχος, ὡς φαρμακοπώλης τὸ μένον σκευάσας
τῆς μετανοίας κολλούριον, ὡς ἁλιεὺς θαλάττης ᾧ οἱ ἰχθύες εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν
ἁλιεύονται–οὗ ἡ σαγήνη λίνον ἔχει τὰ θαύματα, τὰ παθήματα δέλεαρ, ἄγκιστρον τὸν
σταυρὸν καὶ κόλπον τὴν ἀνάστασιν–, ὡς ταμιείου κλειδοῦχος, ἐν ᾧ τοὺς θησαυροὺς
ὁ Πατὴρ ἔχει, τοὺς νυμφῶνας ὁ Υἱός, τὴν τράπεζαν τὸ Πνεῦμα, τὰς χορείας οἱ
ἄγγελοι.
2 Ἀλλὰ Παύλου προστεθέντος, διπλοῦν τὸ τεῖχος καὶ ἁλῶναι μὴ δυνάμενον,
δίστομος ἡ πηγὴ τὴν γῆν ὅλην ἀκαμάτως ποτί ζουσα, διπρόσωπος ἡ λίμνη καὶ πᾶσά
τις ὁλκὰς παραπλέουσα σῴζεται. Τρυγὼν μετὰ χελιδόνος λαλεῖ, περιστερὰ μετὰ τέττι
γος φθέγγεται, αὐλὸς ὁμοῦ καὶ σῦριγξ μέλος ἱερὸν καὶ μειλίχιον ᾄδουσιν.
«Νεανίσκος μετὰ ὁσίου, καὶ εὐθεῖα ἡ ὁδὸς» αὐτῶν, καθάπερ ἐν Παροιμίαις ὁ σοφὸς
ἐκήρυξεν. Ἀμνὸς καὶ λύκος ὁμοῦ νέμονται καὶ ὁ ποιμὴν δοξάζεται καὶ τοῦ
παραδοξοποιητοῦ στε φανοῦται τὰ θαύματα. Ταῦρος καὶ λέων ἐν μιᾷ νομῇ
βόσκονται καὶ τρυγᾷ τοὺς ἐπαίνους ὁ δυναμώσας τὸν ταῦρον καὶ χαλινώσας τὸν
λέοντα. Ἦ οὐχὶ λέων ἐτύγχανεν ὁ Παῦλος ὅτε Σαῦλος ἐτύγ χανεν, ἐπειδὴ φονεύων
τὴν μάνδραν ἐσκόρπιζεν, τοὺς ποιμέ νας κατέπληττεν, ἔσω τῆς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔβρυχεν,
καὶ τὰς πόλεις ἐπτόει, τὰς ἀγορὰς ἐθορύβει, καὶ τοὺς ἀγροὺς ἀοικήτους ἠργά ζετο,
«ἄνδρας σύρων εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ γυναῖκας» δεσμῶν οὐκ ἐπαύετο, πλὴν καὶ τῶν
ἀνδρῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς ἡττᾶτο καὶ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀνδρείας ἀσθενέστερος
ἐτύγχανεν; Ἔτρεχεν εἰκῇ, τὴν γὰρ ὁδὸν οὐκ ἤνυεν· μάτην ἐπύκτευεν, ἐπειδὴ τοὺς
δακτύ λους ᾕμασσεν, εὑρεῖν δὲ οὐχ ὑπῆρχεν ἱκανὸς τὸν ἀντίδικον. Χρι στὸς τοίνυν,
ὡς αὐτὸς σοφός, αὐτὸς καὶ πάλιν ἀγαθὸς παρελθών, τῇ πραότητι κέχρηται καὶ
παραλιπὼν τὰ ὑψηλὰ τὰ ταπεινὰ προβάλλεται. Οὐ τοίνυν ἀνῆψεν πῦρ, οὐκ ἐκίνησεν
λαίλαπας, οὐκ ἐσάλευσεν τῶν ὀρέων τὰ θεμέλια, ἀγγελικὴν οὐκ ἐγύμνωσεν
ῥομφαίαν δίστομον, φωνῇ δὲ πραείᾳ καὶ φιλανθρώπῳ κέκληται· «Σαούλ, Σαούλ»,
λέγων, «τί με διώκεις;» Τίνα σου πλοῦτον ἀφειλάμην; Ποίας σε δόξης ἐγύμνωσα;
thought_title: Peter praised alone, then doubled by Paul
orientation: The preacher begins the homily by praising Peter and then argues that Paul joins him as the second of the pair.
pass_a_gloss: Encomium by Hesychius, elder of Jerusalem, to the holy apostles Peter and Paul. 1 The rose is good, when the spring season offers it to be smelled, but if it is intertwined with the lily it reasonably becomes more fragrant; for perfume is mixed with perfume and a double enjoyment of the fragrance from this comes about. Peter is bright in himself and brighter than the bright, as chief of the apostolic pair, as eye of discipleship, as memorial of zeal and face of faith, as trumpet of the mystery, as tongue and as one who taught many tongues, as shepherd without accusation, as sleepless steersman, as charioteer who does not wander, as seller of drugs who prepared the lasting eye salve of repentance, as fisherman of the sea for whom the fishes are fished up into heaven, whose net has the miracles as line, the sufferings as bait, the cross as hook and the resurrection as embrace, as keeper of the keys of the storehouse, in which the Father has the treasures, the Son the bridal chambers, the Spirit the table, the angels the dances. 2 But with Paul added, the wall is double and unable to be captured, the spring with two mouths waters the whole earth without tiring, the lake with two faces, and every raft sailing past is saved. The turtledove talks with the swallow, the dove utters sound with the cicada, the flute together with the pipe sing a holy and gentle song. A young man with a holy man, and straight is their road, just as in Proverbs the wise man proclaimed. Lamb and wolf graze together and the shepherd is glorified and the wonders of the one who works wonders are crowned. Bull and lion feed in one pasture and he who made the bull strong and bridled the lion gathers the praises. Was Paul not a lion when he was Saul, since by murdering he was scattering the fold, frightening the shepherds, inside Jerusalem he roared, and he frightened the cities, he threw the marketplaces into confusion, and he made the fields uninhabited, he did not stop dragging men into prison and binding women, yet he was being defeated by the endurance of the men and was proving weaker than the courage of the women? He ran in vain, for he did not complete the road; he boxed in vain, since he made his fingers bloody, but he was not able to find the opponent. Christ therefore, as himself wise, himself also again good, having come alongside, uses gentleness and, passing over the high things, puts forward the lowly things. He did not kindle fire, he did not stir whirlwinds, he did not shake the foundations of the mountains, he did not bare the angelic sword with two mouths, but with a gentle and loving voice he has called, saying, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? What wealth of yours did I take away? Of what glory did I strip you?

choices.why: brief glossary requires pair for the apostolic team
brief glossary requires net for the fishing image
brief glossary requires keeper of the keys for Peter as steward
brief glossary requires repentance, not inner change
keeps literal mouth image and avoids polished double jet; avoids hyphen compound

bible_refs.note: quoted source words: ἄνδρας σύρων εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ γυναῖκας
quoted source words: Σαούλ, Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις

pass_b_english: The rose is beautiful, and springtime gives it its scent to breathe. Joined with the lily, it rightly grows still more fragrant. Ointment is mixed with ointment, and the pleasure of the scent is doubled. Peter shines by himself, and he outshines the bright. He is the chief of the apostolic pair, the eye of discipleship, the living record of zeal and the face of faith. He is the trumpet of the mystery, the tongue that taught many tongues, the blameless shepherd, the sleepless pilot, the charioteer who never strays, the pharmacist who prepared the lasting salve of repentance.

He is the fisherman of the sea, and his fish are caught for heaven. His net holds miracles for its threads, sufferings for its bait, the cross for its hook, and the resurrection for its embrace. He is the keeper of the keys of the storehouse where the Father keeps his treasures, the Son his bridal chambers, the Spirit his table, and the angels their dances.

But with Paul added, the wall is doubled and cannot be taken. The spring has two mouths and waters the whole earth without wearying. The lake has two faces, and every vessel sailing past it is saved. The turtledove speaks with the swallow, the dove answers the grasshopper, and the flute and the pipe together sing a holy and gentle song. A young man with a holy man, and their road is straight, as the wise man proclaimed in Proverbs. The lamb and the wolf graze together, and the shepherd is glorified, and the wonders of the wonderworker are crowned. The bull and the lion feed in one pasture, and praises are reaped for the one who gave strength to the bull and bridled the lion. Was not Paul a lion when he was Saul? He scattered the flock by murdering, he terrified the shepherds, he roared inside Jerusalem and frightened the cities. He stirred up the marketplaces and emptied the fields. He never stopped dragging men and women to prison and binding them (Acts 8:3). Yet he was defeated by the endurance of the men and proved weaker than the courage of the women. He ran for nothing, for he did not finish the road. He boxed in vain, for he bloodied his knuckles but could not find his opponent.

So Christ came by, for he is both wise and good. He used gentleness and set aside the high things to put forward the lowly. He did not kindle fire, he did not stir whirlwinds, he did not shake the foundations of the mountains. He did not bare the two-edged sword of an angel. He called with a gentle and loving voice. Christ says, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" (Acts 9:4) What wealth did I take from you? What glory did I strip from you?
notes: Source has broken spacing from printing/OCR, e.g. κορυ φεύς, κυβερνή της, εὐω δίας, ποτί ζουσα, τέττι γος; sense is clear and no text is invented.

problems.quote: Their road runs straight, like youth with a holy man
problems.source_quote: «Νεανίσκος μετὰ ὁσίου, καὶ εὐθεῖα ἡ ὁδὸς» αὐτῶν
problems.why: Νεανίσκος means 'a young man' (Paul), not abstract 'youth', and the Greek has no 'like'; the English turns a Proverbs quotation about the pair into an illogical simile.
problems.fix: "A young man with a holy man, and their road is straight"
problems.ruling: Source quotes «Νεανίσκος μετὰ ὁσίου, καὶ εὐθεῖα ἡ ὁδὸς»; English adds "like" and renders νεανίσκος as abstract youth, garbling the proverb.

edits.old: Their road runs straight, like youth with a holy man, as the wise man proclaimed in Proverbs.
edits.new: A young man with a holy man, and their road is straight, as the wise man proclaimed in Proverbs.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: source Νεανίσκος μετὰ ὁσίου means 'a young man with a holy man', not abstract 'youth', and has no 'like'; restored as quotation about the pair.

last_rejected.quote: dragging men and women to prison and binding them
last_rejected.source_quote: ἄνδρας σύρων εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ γυναῖκας δεσμῶν
last_rejected.why: Greek drags men to prison and binds women; English drags both to prison and binds both.
last_rejected.fix: He never stopped dragging men into prison and binding women.
last_rejected.ruling: Source guillemets («ἄνδρας σύρων εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ γυναῖκας» δεσμῶν) group men and women under σύρων; English follows that valid parsing without misleading readers.

last_rejected.quote: Christ says, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" (Acts 9:4) What wealth did I take from you? What glory did I strip from you?
last_rejected.source_quote: «Σαούλ, Σαούλ», λέγων, «τί με διώκεις;» Τίνα σου πλοῦτον ἀφειλάμην; Ποίας σε δόξης ἐγύμνωσα;
last_rejected.why: Closing the quotation marks after the Acts 9:4 citation leaves Christ's next two questions unquoted, obscuring that Christ is still speaking to Saul.
last_rejected.fix: Christ says, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? (Acts 9:4) What wealth did I take from you? What glory did I strip from you?"
last_rejected.ruling: Greek quotes only «Σαούλ» and «τί με διώκεις»; Τίνα/Ποίας questions lack «». English "I" still identifies Christ as speaker.
